stories.headline: Queen Elizabeth Hospital apologises to patient over ward placement
stories.brief:
The Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has issued an apology after a 79-year-old patient from Tilney St Lawrence reported feeling "frightened and unheard" during her stay last week. Jill Dewsbury, who was admitted with hip pain, claimed she was moved to a ward she believed was for dementia patients, leading her to accuse the hospital of ageist treatment. 

The hospital’s chief nurse, Dawn Collins, has apologised for the distress caused. The trust clarified that the West Dereham ward is not a dementia unit, but cares for older adults with various medical needs. The hospital confirmed it is now reviewing the formal complaint submitted by Mrs Dewsbury.

stories.headline: Looking back at West Norfolk community milestones
stories.brief:
We are taking a look back at local memories from across West Norfolk. In 2011, True’s Yard Museum in King’s Lynn hosted a special event focused on the experiences of wartime evacuees, featuring local volunteer Doris Hanscombe. 

Moving to 2016, plans were progressing for a multi-million-pound heritage rail project based at Wolferton Station. The initiative saw the launch of a new steam locomotive, the Spirit of Sandringham, with the presentation of its official nameplates. These events highlight just a few of the community projects and historical reflections that have taken place in the region over the past decade.

stories.headline: West Norfolk Council defends swimming pool planning costs
stories.brief:
West Norfolk Council is considering spending over £845,000 on the planning stages for new swimming facilities at Lynnsport in King’s Lynn. Council leader Alistair Beales has defended the expenditure as proportionate, citing the high costs of planning in a flood zone and rising construction prices. The proposed project aims to replace the existing St James Swimming Pool, which is currently safe but described as deteriorating.

The Corporate Projects Panel has recommended that the cabinet approve the funding at their next meeting on September 8. However, the council has declined to provide a public breakdown of the costs or reveal the price of extending the life of the current facility. There is no guarantee the new pool will be built.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Town fan fulfils final wish at The Walks
stories.brief:
A lifelong King’s Lynn Town supporter has fulfilled a final wish to watch his team play. Forty-three-year-old James Mason, who is battling a terminal illness, attended Monday’s National League North match against Scarborough Athletic at The Walks. 

Club officials and local supporters helped arrange the visit, which included a presentation of a signed shirt and match ball from players Aaron Jones and Tom Dickens. Mr Mason, who has followed the Linnets since his teenage years, was accompanied by family and friends. The family expressed their gratitude to the club, the hospice charity Tapping House, and Clenchwarton Cabs for providing the transport necessary to make the day possible.

stories.headline: Police appeal for information on wanted man Liam Clarke
stories.brief:
Norfolk Police are searching for 47-year-old Liam Clarke, who is also known as Liam Cook. Officers are looking for him after he failed to attend a scheduled hearing at Norwich Magistrates’ Court. Mr. Clarke is described as five feet nine inches tall with a thin build, short brown hair, and blue eyes. He has known connections to King’s Lynn, Swaffham, and Wisbech.

Anyone with information regarding his current whereabouts is urged to contact the police via their website or by calling the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111. Please quote reference number 35/11070/26 when providing any details.

stories.headline: West Norfolk modellers raise over £2,300 for King’s Lynn Night Shelter
stories.brief:
Members of the West Norfolk International Plastic Modellers’ Society have donated more than £2,300 to the King’s Lynn Night Shelter. The funds were raised during the club’s annual model show held at the Littleport Leisure Centre in June, which attracted 19 traders and over 200 members of the public. 

The charity donation was presented to shelter representatives this past Wednesday. The club, which meets at the William Burt Social Club in West Winch, chooses a local charity to support each year. This latest contribution will assist the shelter, which does not receive government funding, in its ongoing work supporting the homeless across the region.

stories.headline: Queen Elizabeth Hospital addresses service closure concerns
stories.brief:
The Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has issued a statement regarding the future of its services following reports of potential unit closures. The hospital trust confirms that no decisions have been made regarding the future of its Accident and Emergency, intensive care, or maternity departments. 

Officials state they are currently exploring long-term clinical strategies for the Norfolk and Waveney area, but have no preferred options at this stage. The trust says any future proposals for significant service changes would require robust clinical evidence, as well as formal staff and public consultation. The hospital is currently working to address operational challenges as part of a long-term plan for healthcare across the region.

stories.headline: Wisbech Town Council objects to new 24-hour adult gaming centre licence
stories.brief:
Wisbech Town Council has voted unanimously to formally object to a gambling licence application for a proposed 24-hour adult gaming centre at 28 Market Place. The site, a former Halifax Bank that closed in January, received planning permission for a change of use in June.

During Tuesday’s meeting, councillors expressed concerns regarding the potential impact on vulnerable residents, citing the venue's proximity to local support services. Members argued that a third gaming centre in the town could increase the risk of financial harm and acquisitive crime. The formal objection will now be submitted to Fenland District Council for consideration under the Gambling Act 2005.

stories.headline: Wisbech Library to close for five-week refurbishment
stories.brief:
Wisbech Library is set to close at the end of this month for a five-week period to allow for essential building upgrades. During the closure, the site on The Crescent will undergo a series of improvements, including the installation of new air conditioning. 

Further work will focus on the ground floor, where new carpets are to be fitted and a new children’s area will be created. The upcoming project was announced by Councillor Samantha Hoy during a Wisbech Town Council meeting held on Tuesday evening.

stories.headline: Wisbech Mayor reviews recent community engagements
stories.brief:
The Mayor of Wisbech, Councillor Lucie Foice-Beard, has provided an update on her recent community activities during Tuesday’s town council meeting. Over the past month, the Mayor attended several local events, including the town’s Rock Fest and the 150th Wisbech parkrun. She also visited the Wisbech Girls Venture Corps Cadets summer camp and participated in a 16-mile charity walk from Whittlesey to Wisbech to support the Alan Hudson Centre.

Looking ahead, Councillor Foice-Beard highlighted upcoming local events, including the Fenland Food Festival at the Queen Mary Centre this Saturday, Heritage weekends throughout September, and the return of the Wisbech funfair later this month.

stories.headline: Police report August activity in Wisbech
stories.brief:
Neighbourhood officers in Wisbech have reported on their efforts to address drug dealing and anti-social behaviour throughout August. During the month, police conducted 27 stop-searches and made 13 arrests. The operation also resulted in nine drug seizures, with five linked to suspected supply offences, alongside the seizure of three e-bikes and the granting of one partial closure order. Officers additionally filed 40 intelligence submissions while assisting other departments.

The force has invited residents to discuss local concerns at an online community meeting scheduled for 7pm on Tuesday, September 22. Police have thanked the public for sharing information, noting that community reports remain vital to their ongoing work in the town.

stories.headline: Off-road electric bike seized and rider arrested in Wisbech
stories.brief:
Police in Wisbech have seized an off-road electric bike and arrested its rider following a traffic stop on Nene Parade. Fenland response officers spotted the vehicle being driven at speed while they were attending an unrelated incident in the area. 

The rider was arrested on suspicion of driving offences, and the bike was subsequently confiscated. A police spokesperson reminded the public that operating these vehicles on public roads without proper registration, insurance, and a valid licence is illegal. Such offences can result in vehicle seizure, penalty points, and financial fines.

stories.headline: Possible closures of three key units at King’s Lynn’s Queen Elizabeth Hospital discussed
stories.brief:
Senior leaders at the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group are discussing the potential closure of accident and emergency, intensive care, and maternity units at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. The hospital, which serves much of Fenland, is currently part of a long-term strategy review for the county’s three flagship hospitals. 

The group stated that no final decisions have been made and any changes would require public consultation. While the hospital is undergoing a £1.4 billion rebuild, local MPs have expressed differing views on the potential service changes. The hospital group maintains that patients in West Norfolk will continue to have access to urgent and emergency care services on-site.

stories.headline: Wisbech incinerator construction continues as planned
stories.brief:
Construction of the Wisbech incinerator is proceeding according to schedule, eleven months after work began. Current progress includes piling, drainage, and the installation of foundation slabs and walls for the main storage bunker. Two cranes, each approximately 50 metres high, are now visible on the site. Additionally, work has commenced to widen New Bridge Lane.

The Medworth team confirmed that construction will continue throughout the winter, with structural steel work expected to begin in late 2026. While the project faced significant opposition from local councils and campaign groups during the planning stages, including a failed High Court challenge by Fenland District Council, the construction team states that maintaining site cleanliness and keeping neighbours informed remains a priority.

stories.headline: Wisbech cinema announces ticket price cuts for National Cinema Day
stories.brief:
The Light Cinema in Wisbech is reducing ticket prices to £3 for all films throughout this coming weekend. The offer, which runs all day on both Saturday and Sunday, is being held to mark National Cinema Day. 

The schedule includes screenings of Cars, Coyote vs. ACME, and Insidious: Out of the Further, alongside a variety of other titles. Residents are encouraged to visit the cinema’s official website to view the full programme and further details regarding the promotion.
